extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and graduate students working on sphere packing, Voronoi/Delaunay decompositions, and the Kepler conjecture
extracted.subtask_description: Formal construction and analysis of decomposition stars (local configurations around a packing vertex), definition of the scoring function σ, and the reduction of fcc-compatibility to an extremal problem on the compact space DS. Includes all local geometric indexing criteria and piecewise rules used to compute scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: V-cell contains the open unit ball
rubrics_metrics.description: The V-cell at the origin contains the open unit ball at the origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x lies in the open unit ball and is not in the cone over any simplex then the origin is unobstructed and is the closest lattice point, so x ∈ VC(0). If x lies in the cone over a simplex {0,v1,v2,v3} ∈ Q0, then x lies in VC(0) iff it lies in the set bounded by the perpendicular bisectors of vi and the plane through {v1,v2,v3}; verify every point of the convex hull of {v1,v2,v3} has distance at least 1 from the origin (use reflection principle and Lemma 2.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unobstructedness inside B(v,t0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any x ∈ B(v, t0) is unobstructed at v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume a barrier T obstructs x; then every edge of T has distance at least 2 from v and reflection arguments give |v−w| > 2t0 so every point of T has distance at least t0 from v, contradicting x ∈ B(v,t0). Use this to conclude barriers cannot obstruct points inside B(v,t0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local equality of V-cell and Voronoi inside B(0,t0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside the ball of radius t0 at the origin, the V-cell and Voronoi cell coincide: B(0,t0) ∩ VC(0) = B(0,t0) ∩ Ω(0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use unobstructedness (Lemma 3.22) to rule out alternative closest unobstructed vertices within B(0,t0). If x ∈ B(0,t0) ∩ VC(0) ∩ Ω(v) with v ≠ 0, contradiction arises because both v and 0 would be unobstructed and within t0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard regions on the unit sphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Partition the unit sphere by drawing geodesic arcs between radial projections of every pair of vertices v1, v2 for which {0,v1,v2} is a quasi-regular triangle; closures of connected components of the complement are called standard regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A standard region is 'triangular' if bounded by three geodesic arcs and 'non-triangular' otherwise. The arcs meet only at endpoints under the crossing prohibition (Lemma 3.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-crossing of certain edges (lemma 3.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: If v1,v2,v3,v4 satisfy |vi| ≤ 2t0 and |v1−v3|, |v2−v4| ≤ 2t0, then the edges {v1,v3} and {v2,v4} do not cross; in particular the arcs of Definition 3.24 do not meet except at endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geometric inequalities (E(...) bounds) to obtain contradictions if crossing occurs. This ensures the standard-region arcs form a valid partition without interior intersections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplices lie in closed cone over a single standard region
rubrics_metrics.description: Each simplex in the Q-system with a vertex at the origin lies entirely in the closed cone over some standard region R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a simplex had vertices in open cones over two distinct regions, their faces would overlap in forbidden ways (contradict Lemma 3.3). This localizes simplices to single standard regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: V-cell membership inside a simplex (lemma 3.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x lies in the interior of a simplex Q ∈ Q and does not lie on the perpendicular bisector of any edge of Q, then x lies in the V-cell of the closest vertex of Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segments from x to other vertices cross faces that act as barriers, obstructing those vertices; thus only vertices of Q can be unobstructed at x; choose the closest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of barrier triangles B0
rubrics_metrics.description: B0 is the set of triangles T such that either T is a barrier at the origin, or T = {0,v,w} consists of a diagonal of a quarter in the Q-system together with one of its anchors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B0 enumerates the triangular faces relevant to obstruction calculations near the origin; these triangles index faces and walls used by the Decoupling Lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decoupling Lemma (local determination of VC membership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let x ∈ I0 (cube side 4 centered at origin). If the closed segment {x,w} intersects the closed 2D cone over a triangle F ∈ B0, the origin is not obstructed at x, and x is closer to the origin than to both v1 and v2 (vertices of F), then x ∉ VC(w).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lemma shows that, under these local geometric conditions, w cannot be the unique closest unobstructed vertex at x. This permits treating standard regions independently when estimating scoring functions (see Remark 3.30). The proof uses bounded polyhedron X and circumcenter arguments to obtain contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locality of scoring estimates (Remark 3.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Decoupling Lemma permits estimates of the scoring function to be made separately for each standard region; the separate estimates are later reassembled by linear programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because V-cell membership in the cone over a standard region depends only on vertices in the closed cone over that region, scoring contributions are local to regions and can be optimized regionwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing sets I1..I8 for decomposition stars
rubrics_metrics.description: Decomposition stars are encoded by finite indexing sets I1..I8 (and I0) defined relative to an indexing bijection b: ω → Λ; these sets record local adjacencies, quarters, anchors, edges in specified length ranges, face circumradii, and quasi-regular tetrahedra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The eight sets are defined as follows: I1 = ω; I2 = unordered pairs {i,j} with |vi−vj| ≤ 2t0; I3 = unordered tuples whose corresponding simplex is a strict quarter; I4 = unordered tuples whose simplex is in the Q-system; I5 = unordered triples where vi is an anchor of a diagonal of a strict quarter; I6 = pairs with edge length in (2t0, 8); I7 = triples corresponding to triangle faces in Q-system with circumradius < sqrt(2); I8 = unordered quadruples corresponding to quasi-regular tetrahedra with circumradius < 1.41. (These indexing sets may be redundant but are chosen for completeness.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Neighborhood indexing set T (local finiteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given d0 = sqrt(8 + 4/3) (as defined), T = {i : vi ∈ Λ(v,d0)} is the finite indexing set for the neighborhood of v and each restricted indexing set Ij^v = {x ∈ Ij : x ⊂ T} is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decomposition-star data for vertex v consists of f: T → B(0,d0) with f(i)=vi−v together with the tuple of restricted indexing sets (I0^v,...,I8^v). This finite data suffices to reconstruct local geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topology on pairs (f,t) and DS◦
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare (f,t) close to (f',t') iff t=t', domain(f)=domain(f') and f(i) is close to f'(i) for all i in the domain; this descends to an orbit topology on DS◦ (pairs modulo permutations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The topology uses the standard topology on B(0,d0) and discrete topology on finite indexing sets; orbits [f,t] are independent of bijection b:ω→Λ, and DS◦ consists of those orbits arising from saturated packings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactification of DS (closed conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: DS is the compactification of DS◦ obtained by replacing open conditions by closed ones; e.g., if {i,j} ∈ I6 then allow |f(i)−f(j)| to lie in closed interval [2t0,8], etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compactness follows from compactness of B(0,d0), closed conditions on indexing sets, and finiteness of T. Use closed versions of metric inequalities to include degenerate limiting cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition star determines V-cell and Q-simplices (Lemma 4.4 & Cor.4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The V-cell at v depends on Λ only through Λ(v,d0) and the indexing sets Ij; hence there is a canonical V-cell VC(D) attached to each decomposition star D with VC(D)+v = VC(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To decide whether x ∈ Iv belongs to VC(v), one needs only nearby vertices within distance d0 and barrier labels from the decomposition star; intersection points of potential barriers lie within distance ≤ 2/3 from x, so their vertices are in Λ(v,d0).

rubrics_metrics.name: VC(D) is finite union of convex polyhedra and continuous
rubrics_metrics.description: For each decomposition star D, VC(D) is a finite union of nonoverlapping convex polyhedra, and the map D ↦ vol(VC(D)) is continuous on each connected component of DS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On a fixed connected component indexing sets are constant; faces are perpendicular bisector planes or planes through triples of nearby vertices which vary continuously with D, hence volumes vary continuously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voronoi cell depends only on Λ(v,d0) (Lemma 4.7 & Cor.4.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Voronoi cell Ω(v) depends on Λ only through Λ(v,d0); in fact Ω(v) is determined by v and the first indexing set I1 of the decomposition star.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voronoi cell extreme points lie within distance <2 from v by saturation; bisectors from vertices w with dist(w,v)≥4 cannot meet B(v,2), and 4 < d0, so only Λ(v,d0) matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voronoi cell of a decomposition star (Definition 4.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For D ∈ DS, define Ω(D) as the set containing the origin bounded by the perpendicular bisectors of {0,vi} for i ∈ I1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This matches Ω(D(v,Λ)) = v + Ω(v) when D = D(v,Λ). The Voronoi cell volume is recovered directly from the decomposition star's I1 and vertex positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition star encodes all local structures (Remark 4.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: From a decomposition star D one can recover the set U(D) of vertices at distance ≤ 2t0, the set of barriers at the origin, the simplices in the Q-system with a vertex at the origin, the V-cell VC(D), the Voronoi cell Ω(D), and other local data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing sets Ij were chosen specifically to encode these structures; hence all local geometric information required for scoring is present in D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of colored spaces to obtain continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: When σ (or other case-defined functions) is piecewise-defined with discontinuities along degeneracies, form a colored space by duplicating degenerate points into multiple colored components so that σ is continuous on each colored component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret interval endpoints (e.g., x∈[2,2t0]) as carrying the color of the connected component. The decomposition-star indexing sets include cutoffs (e.g., circumradius thresholds) so different cases land in different connected components and continuity is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of A0 (volume correction plus Q-system contributions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A0(D) = −vol(Ω(D)) + vol(VC(D)) + Σ_{Q∈Q0(D)} A1(Q, c(Q,D), 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A0 measures the difference between Voronoi cell volume and V-cell volume plus contributions A1 from simplices in the Q-system attached to the origin. Each A1 depends on the simplex Q, its context c, and a chosen vertex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context of a quarter (Definition 5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quarter Q in Q0(D), its context c(Q,D) is the pair (p,q) where p is the number of anchors and p−q is the number of quarters along the diagonal; q is the number of 'gaps' between anchors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a quarter in a quartered octahedron has context (4,0); a single quarter has context (2,1). Context influences the formula for σ on quarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rogers simplex, quoin and volume building blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: An orthosimplex (Rogers simplex R(a,b,c)) parametrized by a≤b≤c; the quoin quo(R) is the wedge-like solid above R bounded by planes through faces of R and a sphere of radius c at the origin; explicit formulae exist for quo(R) and for vol(VCt(S,v)) via inclusion–exclusion using caps and quoins (Equation 5.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To compute vol(VCt(S,v)) for a simplex S and truncation radius t, start with |S|∩B(v0,t), subtract caps cap_i defined by |x−vi|<|x|, add back intersections which decompose into four quoins each (Lemma 5.4). Use conventions quo(R(a,b,c))=0 if a<b<c fails and vol(capi)=0 if |vi|≥2t to extend formulae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of s-vor and compression Γ(S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define s-vor(S,v,t) = 4( −δ_oct vol VC+_t(S,v) + sol(S,v)/3 ) and s-vor0(S,v) = s-vor(S,v,t0). The compression Γ(S) = (1/4) Σ_{i=1}^4 s-vor(S,vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions combine truncated V-cell volumes and solid angles to produce per-vertex Voronoi-like contributions used in defining σ and A1; Γ(S) is the average 'compression' of the simplex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involution on simplex vertices for quarters (Definition 5.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a simplex Q in the Q-system, define an involution v ↦ ˆv: if Q is a quarter and v is an endpoint of the diagonal, ˆv is the opposite endpoint of the diagonal; otherwise ˆv = v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This involution is used to symmetrize s-vor terms in σ for quarters (averaging contributions from opposite diagonal endpoints where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Piecewise definition of σ and A1 (Definition 5.8 and Equation 5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A1(S,c,v) = −vol VC(S,v) + sol(S,v)/(3δ_oct) − σ(S,c,v)/(4δ_oct), where σ is defined by cases: (1) For a quasi-regular tetrahedron: (a) if circumradius < 1.41 then σ = Γ(S); (b) otherwise σ = s-vor(S,v). (2) For a strict quarter: (a) if η+(S) < sqrt(2): i. context (2,1) or (4,0): σ = Γ(S); ii. other contexts: σ = Γ(S) + (s-vor0(S,v) − s-vor0(S,ˆv))/2. (b) if η+(S) ≥ sqrt(2): i. context (2,1): σ = s-vor(S,v); ii. context (4,0): σ = (s-vor(S,v)+s-vor(S,ˆv))/2; iii. other contexts: σ = (s-vor(S,v)+s-vor(S,ˆv))/2 + (s-vor0(S,v) − s-vor0(S,ˆv))/2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When η+ < sqrt(2) a quarter is called 'compression type' (Γ plays a role); otherwise 'Voronoi type' (s-vor dominates). The piecewise rules depend on circumradius thresholds (1.41 and sqrt(2)) and the context c; these thresholds are encoded in decomposition-star indexing sets so σ is continuous on colored components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of A0 (Lemma 5.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: A0 : DS → R is continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity of volume terms follows from Lemmas 4.6 and similar arguments; σ(S,c,v) appears discontinuous across cutoffs, but those cutoffs are recorded in DS indexing sets (I8, I9, etc.), so different cases inhabit different connected components and continuity holds on DS as a colored/compactified space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing property of A1 over simplex vertices (Lemma 5.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any simplex S in the S-system with context c, the sum of A1 over its four vertices vanishes: Σ_{i=1}^4 A1(S,c,vi) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the algebraic form of A1 and the identities among σ and s-vor terms; s-vor0 terms cancel in sums and the remaining terms are weighted averages that sum appropriately. This cancellation is used later to control boundary contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negligibility condition for functions A:Λ→R
rubrics_metrics.description: A function A:Λ→R is negligible if there exists C1 such that for all r ≥ 1, Σ_{v∈Λ(x,r)} A(v) ≤ C1 r^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negligibility bounds the total contribution of A over balls of radius r by O(r^2). This is the definition used to show that correction functions do not affect density in the Kepler problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof strategy for negligibility of A (Theorem 5.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The function A(v) = A0(D(v,Λ)) is negligible: the proof compares Voronoi and V-cell volumes and uses partition coverings within fixed radii to bound volume differences by O(r^2); contributions from A1 cancel interiorly by Lemma 5.10 and only boundary simplices contribute, which are again O(r^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First bound the sum of −vol(Ω)+vol(VC) over Λ(x,r) by difference of ball volumes (covering/containment) to obtain O(r^2). Then include Σ A1 terms: each simplex contributes to four vertices and cancels unless it straddles the boundary of Λ(x,r), where its number is O(r) and total O(r^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the score σ(D) (Definition 5.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: σ(D) = −4 δ_oct ( vol Ω(D) + A0(D) ) + 16π/3. The score is the affine-rescaled objective function whose maximization over DS corresponds to minimizing vol Ω + A0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: δ_oct and constants are as in earlier definitions; σ is continuous on DS and is the central function to bound (σ(D) ≤ 8 pt) to obtain fcc-compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of minimization and score bound (Lemma 5.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: The extremal statement 'minimize vol Ω(D)+A0(D) on DS' is equivalent to the statement 'maximize σ on DS'; specifically the target bound σ_max = 8 pt is equivalent to the corresponding minimal volume threshold, and either statement implies A is fcc-compatible for every saturated packing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the affine relation between σ and vol Ω + A0 and the identity relating 8 pt to the same affine constants. Thus proving σ(D) ≤ 8 pt for all D ensures fcc-compatibility of the constructed negligible A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of σ bound for fcc-compatibility (Theorem 5.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: If max_{D∈DS} σ(D) = 8 pt, then for every saturated packing Λ there exists a negligible fcc-compatible function A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine the negligibility of A (Theorem 5.11) with the extremal equivalence (Lemma 5.13) to deduce the existence of the desired A for any saturated packing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of σ to standard clusters (section 5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The score σ can be expressed as a sum of terms attached to each standard region (standard cluster) of a decomposition star.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expresses global σ as a sum of local contributions, enabling separate bounding/calculation per standard region and subsequent recombination (used in the large optimization and linear-programming steps). The Decoupling Lemma and the decomposition-star locality underpin this decomposition.
